entities.summary: Quintus Haterius Antoninus was a Roman senator who played a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of the Roman Empire during the reigns of Claudius and Nero. His involvement in the Senate and his connections to powerful figures like Calpurnia and Seneca demonstrate his importance as a mediator between the Emperor and the aristocracy. Despite his relatively minor stature, Antoninus's actions had significant consequences, including the suppression of the Flavian conspiracy and the promotion of the Pax Romana. His legacy is often overshadowed by that of more prominent Roman leaders, but his contributions to the stability and prosperity of the Roman Empire cannot be overstated.
